newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Arjo, Portugal discuss pulp restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Arjo, Portugal discuss pulp restructuring.

text.p: Anglo-French paper manufacturer Arjo Wiggins Appleton Plc is holding talks with the Portuguese government over the restructuring of the pulp and paper sector, Arjo's representative on the board of pulp group Soporcel said.

Arjo holds a 43 percent stake in Portuguese company Soporcel-Sociedade Portuguesa de Celulose, which is 50 percent controlled by state bank Caixa Geral de Depositos (CGD). The remaining seven percent is floated.

"Talks between Arjo Wiggins and the Portuguese government about the restructuring of the paper and pulp sector are continuing," Arjo's representative, Paulo Marques told reporters during the presentation of Soporcel's six-month results.
"We have had a good relationship with the other shareholder (CGD), and talks with the government are continuing," he added.
He gave no details of the talks.

Marques and the president of Soporcel, Alvaro Barreto, said they believed it made sense to invest some 70 billion escudos for the installation of a second paper machine, which will make it possible to transform all pulp production into paper.
"Both shareholders, Arjo and Caixa, continue to support the plan for a complete integration (of pulp production into paper), via the installation of a second paper machine," Barreto said.
Soporcel today announced a six-month first-half net profit of 2.8 billion escudos, compared with a loss of one billion escudos in the first six months of 1996.
